evidence: From the car park at the end of Mt Richmond Road, the track follows the Te Hoiere/Pelorus River for an hour to Emerald Pool, an ideal fishing, swimming and picnicking spot.
Just below Browning Hut cross Browning Stream and walk through a lovely section of forest.
From here it is about an hour to the Hacket roadend and picnic area, through a mixture of plantation and native forests.
Just downstream of this area a suspension bridge crosses the Hacket River from where it's a short walk to the car park.

doubts: The main way is the whole track as the page presents it (Roadend to Hacket picnic area); its start F2 is the Pelorus Track meeting Mount Richmond Road, matching the text's car park at the end of Mt Richmond Road, and its end F1 is taken as the Hacket roadend (the Hacket Track meets Aniseed Valley Road), which the text names as the Hacket car park end. The Roebuck Hut crossing is given as an option: ford on foot or the swingbridge 200 m upstream, so it is recorded as ford. The Exit to Nelson City has its own heading without a time; its end is Brook Street, and the Dun Mountain Trail continues along the old railway line to a point further along Brook Street, which is not walked by that way. The Middy Creek Hut to Rocks Hut and Rocks Hut to The Brook sections have their own times, which are not combined. Time 3-4 days is DOC's summary; no distances for the main way. The Rocks Hut to Tōtara Saddle, Maungatapu and Mt Fell entries sit under 'Other tracks' or as a route off this track and are not ways for this walk.
